bull.b: Completing dosing advances CDI-988 from enrollment into a results-generating stage, creating a defined clinical catalyst and testing the candidate’s potential in prevention and treatment. The program’s oral format and focus on an underserved norovirus market could support future differentiation if efficacy is demonstrated.

The $5 million placement strengthens near-term resources for clinical development and signals continued support from an existing strategic investor. That funding can help sustain antiviral programs through upcoming data milestones, although it does not yet represent recurring operating revenue.

Adding a director with experience in antiviral therapy and prior FDA approvals can improve oversight of clinical and regulatory decisions. Her expertise is particularly relevant as CDI-988 advances and may strengthen strategic guidance across Cocrystal’s broader antiviral pipeline.

bear.b: Cocrystal remains far from a self-sustaining commercial model: revenue is small relative to operating losses, and profitability is deeply negative. This cost structure means continued dependence on external funding while candidates progress, limiting financial resilience over the next several quarters.

Although cash burn has improved from 2024, operating and free cash flow remain firmly negative and closely track net losses. Continued outflows consume available resources before products generate scalable inflows, increasing the likelihood that additional financing will be needed to fund development.

bear.t: Thinner and more leveraged balance sheet
bear.b: The contraction in assets and shift to debt exceeding equity leave Cocrystal with a thinner financial buffer than in prior years. Higher leverage alongside ongoing losses can reduce flexibility to absorb setbacks or finance clinical programs without relying on further capital.
